topic: Atoms are about 99.9999999% empty space: squeeze the empty space out of every human on Earth and we would fit into a sugar cube
title: All 8 Billion Humans Can Fit in a Sugar Cube
description:
Atoms are over 99.9999999% empty space. If you squeezed out all that empty space, every person on Earth would fit inside a single sugar cube!

#shorts #science #physics

Video by AlexKopeykin on Pixabay
Video by Hans on Pixabay
Video by Kaffeesüchtig on Pixabay
Video by Kanenori on Pixabay
Video by Leolo212 on Pixabay
Video by ThomaLutfpv on Pixabay
Video by olexlia on Pixabay
Video by u_g0anzkkvlg on Pixabay
Video by u_u6puzc3oy8 on Pixabay
hook: Right now, your entire body is mostly empty space.
question: So if atoms are mostly empty, why do your feet stop on the floor instead of falling right through? What force is pushing back? Tell me your guess below!
answer_comment: The answer: The Pauli Exclusion Principle and electromagnetic forces! Electrons cannot occupy the same quantum state. When the electron clouds in your shoes and the floor overlap, quantum mechanics forces them into higher energy states, generating immense repulsive resistance. You're essentially levitating on a tiny cushion of electromagnetic repulsion governed by the Pauli Exclusion Principle! What crazy physics fact should we explore next?

title: Your Gut Is A Second Brain

hook: You have a second brain, and it’s not in your head.
question: So, if your gut communicates directly with your brain, why do you think you lose your appetite when you are extremely nervous?
answer_comment: The answer: When you are stressed, your brain triggers a fight-or-flight response. This diverts blood away from your digestion to your muscles, essentially shutting down your stomach to save energy for the perceived danger. It's your body's way of prioritizing survival over digestion! Does this happen to you before big events?

topic: Why does ice float when almost every other solid sinks in its own liquid
title: Why Does Ice Float?
description:
Ever wonder why ice cubes float instead of sinking? It comes down to the unique way water molecules behave when they freeze. Explore the science of density! #science #physics #shorts

Video by Afzaal0001 on Pixabay
Video by Hans on Pixabay
Video by Kaffeesüchtig on Pixabay
Video by Kanenori on Pixabay
Video by MilanWulf on Pixabay
Video by Razzak_100 on Pixabay
Video by RoyBuri on Pixabay
hook: Many things shrink when they freeze, but water is one of the few that actually expands.
question: Ever thought how this trick of nature keeps fish alive in a frozen lake?
answer_comment: The answer: Because ice is less dense than water, it forms a solid layer on the surface of the lake. This top layer of ice actually acts like a blanket, insulating the deeper water from the freezing air above. This keeps the water below the ice liquid, so fish can swim through the winter. Pretty cool, right? Got another question about the states of matter?

topic: Why do onions make you cry when you cut them
title: Why Onions Make You Cry
description:
Ever wonder why chopping onions turns you into a blubbering mess? It is not just you—it is actual chemistry at work. Find out how plants defend themselves and how a simple temperature trick can save your eyes.

#science #onions #shorts

Photo by Alexas_Fotos on Pixabay
Photo by EME on Pixabay
Photo by Storme22k on Pixabay
Photo by VIVIANE6276 on Pixabay
Photo by Vierschilling on Pixabay
Photo by neelam279 on Pixabay
Photo by olleaugust on Pixabay
Video by klimkin on Pixabay
hook: You are not sad when you chop an onion.
question: Ever thought why keeping the root attached helps you cry less? Drop your guess below.
answer_comment: The answer: The root area of the onion has the highest concentration of the enzymes that trigger the gas reaction. By cutting around the root and leaving it for last, you release far less gas into the air while you chop most of the bulb. Did you try this trick at home yet? Let us know!

question: Ever thought why a sharp knife makes you cry less than a dull one?

topic: Why Noise-Canceling Headphones Don't Block Sound—They Blast 'Anti-Sound' Into Your Ears
title: How Noise Canceling Actually Works
description:
Ever wonder how your headphones make silence? It’s not a physical wall, but a clever trick with sound waves. See how we turn noise into nothing. #shorts #science #physics

Photo by ClickerHappy on Pixabay
Photo by Drumcliff on Pixabay
Photo by Sunriseforever on Pixabay
Photo by adonyig on Pixabay
Photo by congerdesign on Pixabay
Photo by k_seergeevna on Pixabay
hook: Noise-canceling headphones don't just rely on thick foam...
question: Ever thought why your noise-canceling headphones struggle to silence someone talking to you right next to you?
answer_comment: The answer: Noise cancellation works best on consistent, low-frequency sounds like airplane engines. Human speech is fast, unpredictable, and changes pitch constantly. Because the microphone can't predict the exact shape of your friend's voice in time to create the perfect opposite wave, the sound gets through! Want to know how we might fix that? Ask away.

title: Why You Kick While Falling Asleep
description:

hook: You just fell asleep, and suddenly, your body kicks as if you’re falling off a cliff.
question: Ever thought why these jerks happen more often when you are exhausted or stressed?
answer_comment: The answer: When you are exhausted, your brain transitions from wakefulness to deep sleep much faster than usual. Researchers think this rapid shift might confuse your nervous system, making it more likely to trigger a sudden spasm. It's essentially a 'system error' caused by an accelerated sleep onset. hook: Mirrors reflect light straight back, but because we imagine turning around to face ourselves, our reflection appears to swap left and right.
question: Ever thought why a cardboard arrow pointing right still points right when you spin it on a table? Drop your guess below.
answer_comment: The answer: Spinning the arrow on a table rotates it around a vertical axis in the same plane, so it never reverses front-to-back the way you do when facing a mirror. Because it only rotates sideways, an arrow pointing right stays pointing right from your perspective. What happens if you flip the arrow face down instead?

topic: Why Drinking Cold Water Makes Spicy Food Burn WORSE
title: Why Ice Water Makes Spicy Food Burn Worse
description:
Drinking ice water after eating spicy food feels like a good idea, but science says it makes the burn worse. Here is why that happens. #shorts #science #spicy

Photo by Alexandra_Koch on Pixabay
Photo by Bru-nO on Pixabay
Photo by Pezibear on Pixabay
Photo by Storme22k on Pixabay
Photo by cgdsro on Pixabay
Photo by markusspiske on Pixabay
hook: Drinking cold water makes spicy food burn worse.
question: Ever thought why fatty foods like peanut butter help put out a chili fire better than soda?
answer_comment: The answer: Capsaicin is an oil-based chemical, so water just moves it around your mouth instead of washing it away. Peanut butter contains fats that can help trap the capsaicin oil and remove it from your tongue, similar to how milk works. Soda is mostly water and carbonation, which spreads the oil around even more. Got another spicy food myth you want tested?
